collection.credit:
CHATGPT-WRITTEN EVENTS — WITH LORSIEAB2 CREATIVE DIRECTION
* VV5 woodworking showcase, potluck dispute, laundry misunderstanding,
  neighborly games, keeper of little things and festival events:
  event prose/branches by ChatGPT; overarching VV5 two-community setup,
  Guardians of Harmony naming and gameplay constraints by Lorsieab2.

ledger.why: the Building or Research effect on w3 (the labeling system)

items.text: a shirt with far too many sleeves
a cloak covered in decorative patches
a cloth bag embroidered with flowers
The item is returned. The neighbors share a friendly conversation and go about their day.
(Finder) and the Isolan visitor exchange sewing tips.
The owner is embarrassed but grateful. "I was looking everywhere for that!"
A villager suggests a grand annual laundry festival. The others firmly reject the proposal.
The incident becomes a small joke between the communities. Nothing more dramatic comes of it.

intro.name: The basket
intro.text:
A basket of freshly washed clothing has appeared between the two communities. Unfortunately, nobody knows who owns it.
(Finder) discovers {A} among the laundry.
An Isolan visitor insists that the item belongs to (isolan.his/her) community. (Claimer) insists it belongs to the village.

ask.name: Whose is it
ask.text: The problem is that neither can actually prove it.

choices.label: Hold the item until someone claims it.
Put on an impromptu fashion show to find the owner.

a1.text: The owner is found immediately. Everyone apologizes for the confusion.

a2.text: Several villagers claim the item, each with a surprisingly convincing explanation.

a3.text: The real owner admits (owner.he/she) left the item behind after visiting the other community.

s1.text: An elder recognizes the distinctive stitching and identifies the owner.

s2.text: The pattern is common to both communities. The villagers discover they have been sharing techniques for years.

s3.text: A child recognizes the item because (kid.he/she) accidentally sewed one sleeve on backward.

w1.text: The owner arrives the next morning, grateful that the item was kept safe.

w2.text: Nobody claims it. The villagers agree to store it until the next gathering.

w3.text: The two communities decide to make a simple system for labeling shared laundry.

show.text: (Finder) declares that the easiest way to identify the owner is to have volunteers model the mysterious garment.

f1.text: The true owner laughs and claims it immediately.

f2.text: The garment is far too small for the volunteer. The crowd applauds the effort anyway.

f3.text: The Isolan visitor reveals that the item is actually a tablecloth. The volunteer slowly removes it.

f4.text: A child announces that the garment belongs to the village's laundry basket. Nobody finds this helpful.
